children: Egyptian developer Marsoum Developments is targeting around 50 billion Egyptian pounds ($973.5 million) in investments for The Central Gate, a new 80-feddan mixed-use development in October Gardens, West Cairo.
The project will comprise residential units, a hotel, medical complex, administrative and commercial facilities, green spaces and other supporting services, the company said in a press statement.
The residential portion will include apartments starting from 74 square metres (sqm), alongside two- and three-bedroom units and duplexes, the statement said.
The Central Gate marks Marsoum’s second development in Egypt after EGP 20 billion ($389 million) Smouha Gate in Alexandria.

Chairman Ayman Embabi said the project forms part of the company's expansion strategy in Egypt, with October Gardens selected because of its development potential and connectivity to key areas of West Cairo.
Marsoum said West Cairo is a key area for expansion plans, supported by infrastructure development and demand for integrated residential communities.
Sayed Saber, Executive Board Member added that the project’s location, diversified units, mixed-use model and flexible payment plans are The Central Gate’s most attractive elements.
He said residential units will start at EGP 1.8 million ($35 million), with payment plans starting from a 5 percent down payment and installments extending for up to 12 years.
(Writing by Marwa Abo Almajd; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Egypt’s Marsoum targets over $973mln investment in West Cairo mixed-use project
